transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-12; Start: 15:00 UTC; Duration: 48m; Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maria (MedInnovate Head of AI), Ethan (CTO), Priya (Data Lead), Noah (SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Uh quick agenda — scoping the POC quality eval plan, make sure we have success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines. Sound good?
[00:12] Dr. Maria: Yep, sounds good. Thanks Samir.
[00:15] Ethan: Morning all. We're pretty tight on timeline — board wants initial results in 6 weeks, so need to be realistic.
[00:22] Lena: Got it, we'll propose a schedule that fits. First question on success criteria: do you want strict numeric SLOs, or more qualitative pass/fail on categories?
[00:33] Priya: For us quantitative matters — we want F1-ish metrics on entity extraction (clinical terms), hallucination rate under 2% on summaries, and 95% format fidelity for our structured output. But we also need human-rated quality for triage items.
[00:48] Samir: That's helpful. To confirm, success criteria proposed: (1) entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our sample set; (2) hallucination rate < 2% measured on golden prompts; (3) format fidelity (JSON schema compliance) >= 95%; (4) human utility score average >= 4/5 on review set. Are we aligned?
[01:10] Dr. Maria: Yes. Also want latency considerations — if we go hosted we need median latency < 350ms for short responses, and < 800ms for longer summarizations — if dedicated, we can relax a bit but cost matters.
[01:26] Lena: We'll include latency/cost tradeoff buckets in the benchmark. We'll run both hosted and a dedicated instance for comparison where feasible.
[01:36] Noah: For networking we probably need VPC peering and allowlist for egress, we can't have open egress to public internet. SOC2 and encryption in transit and at rest are musts.
[01:47] Samir: Noted — we'll include SOC2 report and KMS/HSM details in the security packet.
[01:52] Marcus: Also capture audit log retention expectations, that's usually a blocker for enterprise.
[01:57] Ethan: Yes, 12-month audit retention is required.
[02:02] Lena: On the eval plan specifics: we recommend a two-track quality evaluation — automated scoring against golden prompts + regression test suite, and a human-in-the-loop review for edge cases and hallucination analysis.
[02:17] Priya: Can you expand on golden prompts? We're thinking a set of 50-100 prompts that represent typical calls and clinical notes.
[02:26] Lena: Exactly. Golden prompts are a curated set that cover the distribution: short clinical facts, multi-paragraph encounter summaries, A/B test prompts that may cause hallucinations, and complex extraction requests. We'll score model outputs against expected outputs — token-level F1 for entities, exact-match for fields in the schema, and bag-of-words similarity for summaries where appropriate.
[02:48] Dr. Maria: How do you handle partial matches? For example, if the model returns an abbreviation or slightly different phrasing?
[02:54] Samir: We'll use normalized string matching and synonyms map — Priya, if you can provide your list of canonical terms that helps. We'll include soft matching thresholds to avoid false negatives.
[03:07] Priya: Yes, we'll provide synonyms and preferred terms.
[03:10] Lena: For hallucination checks, we'll have explicit hallucination prompts where the ground truth is empty or 'no information' and measure false positive assertions. We'll tag hallucination types: fabrication, attrition, hallucinated dates, and so on.
[03:27] Noah: For format fidelity we need strict JSON schema validation; even small deviations break downstream systems.
[03:33] Lena: We'll run a validator and report percent passing. We'll also include auto-correct suggestions counts — how often the model needs a small edit versus a structural fix.
[03:43] Samir: On regression tests — we'll snapshot baseline model behavior and run nightly comparison during the POC. If any metric drops beyond a threshold we'll flag as regression.
[03:53] Dr. Maria: Which baseline model will we use?
[03:56] Lena: We usually use a current open model we've validated internally — we can also use your internally validated variant if you want. For fairness we'll run Redwood-verified baseline + one tuned variant.
[04:08] Ethan: Cost is a big factor. Can you provide token cost per thousand and an estimate given our workload?
[04:15] Samir: Yes — once we have sample workload we'll produce cost buckets. For sizing, Priya can share 3 weeks of anonymized logs — we need average request size, 95th percentile length, and concurrency.
[04:29] Priya: I can drop that in by end of week. We have around 12k requests/day right now, average 120 tokens, 95th ~900 tokens, peak concurrency around 40.
[04:40] Samir: Great, that's enough to do a first cost estimate. We'll simulate at those sizes in the benchmark.
[04:46] Lena: Benchmark approach: 1) Golden prompt run (50-100 canonical prompts) for correctness and hallucination; 2) Synthetic replay of 3 weeks sample traffic for throughput/latency/cost; 3) Regression suite of 200+ prompts derived from historical edge cases; 4) Human review panel of ~100 outputs for utility scoring.
[05:07] Dr. Maria: For the human panel, do you recruit annotators or do we provide SMEs?
[05:12] Marcus: We can do both; we recommend at least 10 SME reviews from your team for high-impact categories. We can also provide our annotation partner for broader coverage.
[05:23] Priya: We'll allocate 3 SMEs initially.
[05:26] Samir: Timeline proposal: Day 0 (receipt of samples + golden prompts) -> 3 business days to confirm config -> Week 1 run golden prompts and baseline -> Week 2 run full replay and regression -> Week 3 human review and analysis -> Week 4 results and recommendation. Given your board timeline we can compress to 3 weeks if customer provides artifacts immediately.
[05:49] Ethan: Can you compress Week 2 and Week 3? If we have the samples tomorrow we can prioritize.
[05:55] Lena: We can compress but will need parallel runs and more infra — that changes cost. We'll quote both standard and expedited timelines.
[06:05] Dr. Maria: Good. On benchmarks — do you run on our VPC/private deployment or in Redwood hosted environment?
[06:12] Samir: We prefer hosted for speed, but we can run the same harness against a private deployment if you want to see parity. For private, we need networking access and an image or instance to run against.
[06:23] Noah: We prefer private for PHI concerns; on-prem or VPC peering. We can do a temporary peering for the benchmark.
[06:30] Lena: We'll provide instructions for running local runner in your VPC and can ingest results back. If egress is restricted, results can be uploaded to a presigned S3.
[06:41] Dr. Maria: About scoring approach — please detail how you combine metrics into a single POC score.
[06:48] Lena: We'll produce a multi-dimensional dashboard and an aggregate score. Proposed weights: correctness/entity F1 40%, hallucination penalty 25% (lower is better), format fidelity 15%, human utility 20%. We can tune weights to your priorities.
[07:03] Priya: That sounds reasonable; maybe bump entity F1 to 45 and human utility to 25 for us.
[07:09] Samir: Noted — we'll provide a configurable scoring sheet.
[07:14] Ethan: How do you measure hallucination penalty numerically?
[07:18] Lena: We compute hallucination rate as fraction of outputs that contain unsupported assertions in hallucination prompts and weight by severity. The penalty is non-linear — e.g., major clinical fabrication leads to bigger score hits. We'll document taxonomy.
[07:32] Dr. Maria: Will you provide explainability traces? We want token attributions or confidence bands.
[07:38] Lena: For some models we can provide logit-based confidence and attention traces but it's limited. We can surface model uncertainty heuristics and where the KV cache may have affected outputs. Note: sometimes transcription or transcript said 'KV cash' but we mean KV cache in runtimes.
[07:54] Samir: Important to mention: we'll include prompts for format-enforced responses with tool-calling or wrapper JSON schema. That helps reduce structural errors.
[08:03] Priya: Are function calls supported in your hosted environment?
[08:07] Lena: Yes, we support structured tool-calling and function schema enforcement; we'll include examples.
[08:13] Ethan: For regression detection — what thresholds will trigger an automatic alert?
[08:18] Lena: Default is a relative drop of >5% in a core metric (e.g., F1) or absolute hallucination increase >1 percentage point; we can adjust.
[08:27] Marcus: Also we flag any schema noncompliance >2% as critical.
[08:31] Dr. Maria: On edge cases, can we add custom checks, e.g., PHI masking and HIPAA redaction tests?
[08:38] Samir: Absolutely — we can include a PHI detection/regression test to ensure the model doesn't leak identifiers and that redaction rules apply.
[08:46] Priya: Good. We'll supply sample documents with redacted fields.
[08:50] Lena: About score aggregation: we'll deliver raw metric CSVs, dashboards, and a one-page executive summary showing pass/fail and recommendations (e.g., quantize, fine-tune, routing to a larger model for edge cases).
[09:05] Ethan: If results are borderline, what are typical next steps?
[09:09] Samir: Options are: small fine-tune on your golden set, prompt engineering and schema enforcement, or route high-risk prompts to a higher-quality model at higher cost. We'll include cost/benefit in our report.
[09:22] Dr. Maria: Fine. Security checklist — we need SAML SSO, role-based access, and KMS integration.
[09:30] Marcus: We'll include SSO docs and KMS flow. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS in supported clouds.
[09:38] Noah: Does Redwood keep any customer data for training? We can't allow training on PHI.
[09:43] Samir: No, Redwood does not use customer data to train models by default; we have a strict policy and can sign contractual language. We'll include the clause.
[09:52] Priya: Ok. A couple of clarifying items on workload sizing: our 12k req/day estimate — are you able to run concurrency at 40 and simulate spikes of double that?
[10:03] Lena: Yes, we'll simulate peak 2x concurrency and measure latency percentiles and tail latency. We'll also test batching behavior and the impact of KV cache on repeated requests.
[10:16] Dr. Maria: Please check long-context behavior — our notes can be up to 8k tokens.
[10:21] Lena: We'll include long-context benchmarks; note that performance and cost change nonlinearly with context length. We'll include sequence-length specific profiles.
[10:31] Ethan: Any limitations around quantization or specialized hardware for private instances?
[10:36] Lena: We support quantized variants; on certain hardware we can run 4-bit/8-bit. We'll document expected quality delta and cost savings.
[10:47] Samir: We'll include recommended quantization profiles per workload.
[10:50] Priya: For the golden prompt set — should we include negative prompts where model should say "I don't know"?
[10:56] Lena: Yes, negative/no-info prompts are crucial for hallucination detection. We'll include ~20% of golden prompts as no-info or contradictory content.
[11:05] Dr. Maria: For human evaluation, what rubric do you use?
[11:09] Marcus: We use a clear rubric: correctness (0-5), completeness (0-5), hallucination severity (0-3), format compliance (pass/fail), and overall utility 1-5. We provide annotator instructions and examples.
[11:23] Priya: Will you provide inter-annotator agreement scores?
[11:27] Marcus: Yes, we'll compute Cohen's kappa or similar and surface notes on ambiguous cases.
[11:34] Samir: On deliverables — we'll provide: benchmark workbook (CSV), dashboard link, executive summary, raw logs (anonymized), and recommendations.
[11:41] Dr. Maria: Great. One procedural ask: include a lightweight plan for A/B testing during pilot after POC.
[11:47] Lena: We'll include canary and A/B rollout suggestions with routing policies — e.g., route 5% to candidate, monitor metrics for 48 hours, then escalate.
[11:58] Ethan: Any special legal paperwork we need to sign before sharing sample PHI? NDA? BAA?
[12:04] Samir: We'll provide our standard BAA and can sign a mutual NDA; Marcus will attach the BAA with the security packet.
[12:13] Priya: Thanks. A question on evaluation environment parity — results can differ between hosted and private. How do you normalize?
[12:21] Lena: We'll run the same harness and seed where possible; we'll capture environment metadata and annotate differences. If results diverge, we'll do a root-cause (kernel, quantization, GPU driver, batching).
[12:34] Dr. Maria: Okay. Anything else we should cover?
[12:38] Samir: Quick recap and next steps.
[12:40] Samir: Action items we captured: Samir send pricing, SOC2, BAA; Lena send benchmark workbook and scripts; Priya provide samples and golden prompts; Noah confirm VPC details; Marcus schedule follow-up. Targeting first benchmark run week of 2026-03-23.
[12:58] Dr. Maria: That aligns. We'll try to provide artifacts by 2026-03-16 to enable the compressed schedule.
[13:04] Ethan: One last thing — competitor concerns: we're evaluating whether to keep some workflows on our internal on-prem pipeline vs Redwood hosted. We'll need clear tradeoffs in cost and SLA.
[13:15] Samir: We'll include a comparison table in the executive summary.
[13:19] Priya: Thanks all.
[13:21] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with packets and links.
[13:25] Lena: Bye.
[13:26] Marcus: Bye.

Note: Transcript contains natural speech artifacts, occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cache sometimes heard as KV cash), and speaker overlap.
